name: Mali

latest_census.notes: 4e RGPH, April 2009. Language is certain: the repo already reads Tableau S-3 'Population Résidente de 6 Ans et Plus Selon la Langue' by region from the USCB/HDX workbook. Religion and ethnicity are recalled as also on the 2009 questionnaire (the 1998 and 2009 reports give a Muslim share around 90-95%), with medium confidence -- the USCB workbook carried only the language sheet, which is weak evidence either way. A 5th RGPH was prepared (cartography from 2022) but I do not know that enumeration has taken place; treat 2009 as latest until the runner sees otherwise on instat-mali.org.

subnational_sources.title: Mali Subnational Population and Housing Data Tables with Administrative Boundaries (USCB via HDX) -- Tableau S-3 language, regions only (already built)
subnational_sources.matches_boundary_level: admin1 (9/9 filled); the 50 cercles are listed but blank
subnational_sources.evidence: The repo's own adapter (scripts/fetch_census/uscb.py, MALI) and docs/SOURCES.md; slug copied from the adapter.

subnational_sources.title: RGPH 2009 -- Résultats définitifs / analytical volumes (Tome 'État et structure de la population' and socio-cultural characteristics) by region and cercle
subnational_sources.matches_boundary_level: admin1 (9) and admin2 (50 cercles: Bougouni, Goundam, Niafunké, Yélimané ... as drawn)
subnational_sources.evidence: Recalled: INSTAT published the 2009 definitive results as PDF volumes with tables by region and cercle; religion and ethnicity tables by region are what I expect there. Exact volume title and URL not certain. The cercle-level language table would fill what the USCB sheet left blank.

subnational_sources.title: Afrobarometer Round 9 (already built: fills 7 of 9 admin1 regions; two thin regions dropped by the MIN_SAMPLE rule)
subnational_sources.evidence: Packet: religion 7, ethnicity 7 of 9 from an adapter; the Afrobarometer adapter covers MLI (code 21). Any 2009 census religion/ethnicity table by region supersedes it.

subnational_sources.title: Enquête Démographique et de Santé du Mali 2018 (EDSM-VI) -- respondents by religion and ethnic group, by region
subnational_sources.evidence: The packet's national ethnicity shares (Bambara 33.3%, Fulani 13.3% ...) are the 2018 DHS figures. A survey of women and men 15-49, not a count; listed below the census and below nothing else.

tier_reason: Language by region is already built from the machine-readable USCB workbook; the remaining prizes -- religion and ethnicity by region from the 2009 census, and any field by cercle -- exist only in INSTAT PDF volumes whose titles and URLs I cannot give with certainty.
recommended_action: Crawl instat-mali.org for the RGPH 2009 'résultats définitifs' volumes; read religion and ethnicity by region (9 = admin1) to replace the Afrobarometer shares and fill Kidal/whichever two regions the survey dropped; read language (and, if present, religion/ethnicity) by cercle for the 50 blank admin2 shapes. Also check whether RGPH5 has been enumerated. Hazard: Mali's 2023 reorganisation into 19 regions -- the boundary file and the 2009 tables share the old 8 regions + Bamako frame, so use 2009-frame tables only.
not_found: Certainty that religion and ethnicity were on the 2009 questionnaire (medium confidence only)
Any machine-readable cercle-level table (the USCB workbook lists the cercles blank)
summary: Mali's 2009 census language table by region is already built from the USCB/HDX workbook (9/9 admin1) and its cercle rows are blank there. Religion and ethnicity currently come from the Afrobarometer survey (7 of 9 regions) and would be superseded by the 2009 census tables that INSTAT published as PDF volumes by region and cercle. Tier B: the count exists on paper, not in a file I can name.
